myths.title: Name and Meaning
myths.text: The name means "The ruler of Laṅkā and chief of the Rākṣasas, whose destruction by Rāmacandra forms the subject of the Rāmāyaṇa" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Rāvaṇa appears within the Sanskrit tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Rāvaṇa continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Sanskrit tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Rāvaṇa embodies ten-headed king, lanka in the Sanskrit imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Rāvaṇa is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Sanskrit tradition.
